clue.text: Abandoning backwoods, I'm often out on the tiles

definitions.text: I'm often out on the tiles

parts.note: scrubbing a plan means abandoning or cancelling it
brush is scrubby wooded country, the backwoods

explanation.surface: A rustic who has quit the backwoods boasts of nights out partying in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out on the tiles' suggests a night of revelry; read literally, it is where a floor scrubber works.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff floor-cleaning tool spends much of its life out on tiled kitchen and bathroom floors.

clue.text: Colourful stuff from dodgy transparencies AA sent out

indicators.note: dodgy suggests the letters are unsound and get rearranged
the two As are sent out of the word transparencies before the rest is shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that suspect slides were posted by the motoring organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' removes the two As from TRANSPARENCIES, leaving TRNSPRENCIES, and 'dodgy' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints made by forcing ink through a stencilled mesh are often bright, boldly coloured images.

clue.text: Direct lines to centre one added to incomplete set?

indicators.note: incomplete means the set loses its final letter

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about completing a set by adding one more piece, with lines aimed at the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In a circle the straight segments running from the rim to the middle are its spokes in geometry.

clue.text: Traditional words before play interrupt each session

parts.note: to break something off is to interrupt it
a, as in ten pounds a head, means each
a leg is one session or stage of a contest, as in darts

explanation.surface: A theatre ritual: customary words spoken before a performance that break up each sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors wish each other luck before a performance with this superstitious idiom instead of saying 'good luck'.

clue.text: Grandly taking over diocese at end of this month

indicators.note: at end of places the reversed diocese after the month abbreviation

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

indicators.note: over tells us the diocese name is turned back to front

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city and diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop grandly takes charge of a diocese at the end of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with grandeur and flourish is to do it lavishly and fashionably, an idiom for showiness.

clue.text: Butcher's relaxed into G&S role at last

indicators.note: into says the word for relaxed goes inside the initials

parts.note: G and S, the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan
limp means slack or relaxed

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of role

explanation.surface: A performer eases into a Gilbert and Sullivan part as a butcher, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look, so 'have a butcher's' means take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang butcher's hook gives look, and a quick look is a brief sighting.

clue.text: Drifts round, hemmed in by sheep

indicators.note: hemmed in by puts the round letter inside the sheep

parts.note: rams are male sheep
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something drifts in circles, penned in by a flock of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander aimlessly without fixed course is to drift, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fifties' musical a beginner put on in States

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the word for states

parts.note: says means states, as a verb
L is for learner, a beginner
to put something on is to add it

explanation.surface: A 1950s show staged with a novice in the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' is not the USA but the verb, SAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Slade's hit stage show opened in 1954, a light British musical of that decade.

clue.text: Retiring say, after Republican papers fold

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the other two

parts.note: ID, identity papers

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for say is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A shy person, after a Republican newspaper folds, retires from public life.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised crease or crest in a surface is a fold or crinkle, as in a ridged fabric.

clue.text: Initially so passive, I perk up as spring goes on

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: to rally is to perk up or recover

explanation.surface: Someone passive at first perks up as springtime goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a coiled wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil spring winds round in a helix, so it runs in a winding, corkscrew fashion.

clue.text: Careless teen surprisingly a favourite with audience

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A careless teenage actor surprisingly wins over the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who draws all attention from the lead becomes the audience's darling, upstaging others.

clue.text: Close to safe area in hazardous Scottish island

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of safe
in puts the area letter inside the word for hazardous

parts.note: risky means hazardous

explanation.surface: Near a safe spot within a hazardous Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: ERISKAY is a small island in the Outer Hebrides, famous for the wreck of the SS Politician.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small Hebridean isle off the west coast of Scotland, south of South Uist.

clue.text: Researcher's mail counter paid for on delivery

parts.note: post means mail

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: COD, cash on delivery

explanation.surface: An academic's post arrives at a counter, paid for on delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who has finished a doctorate and does research on a fixed contract holds a postdoctoral post.

clue.text: Pontifical comrade coming round every year

indicators.note: coming round says the comrade goes round the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: a pal is a comrade
pa, per annum, means every year

explanation.surface: A pompous friend comes calling every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Pope, the Pontiff, the Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Cromwell's bodyguard?

parts.note: Oliver Cromwell ruled as Lord of the Commonwealth with this title; a bodyguard is one who shields another

explanation.surface: A question about who guarded Oliver Cromwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's title was Lord Protector, and a bodyguard is literally someone who guards a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell's official title and the plain word for a minder who keeps someone safe are the same word.

clue.text: Coach following Everton's lead certainly causes tension for viewers

indicators.note: following puts the coaching word after the other pieces
lead takes the leading letter of Everton's

parts.note: yes means certainly
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A football coach following Everton's lead causes tension for the club's spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; 'viewers' are eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes after long staring are a strain on those who look, viewers being eyes.

clue.text: Taiwan's top philosopher accumulated household items for union

indicators.note: top takes the first letter of Taiwan's

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, the French philosopher

explanation.surface: A leading Taiwanese thinker collects goods for a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is a marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of linen, clothes and goods gathered for married life is her bottom drawer.

clue.text: Popular journal one catholic finds 'lifeless'

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
an organ is a journal or official publication
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A popular Catholic magazine is found to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter not derived from living things, such as minerals, has no life in it.

clue.text: What bowler aims at from square leg?

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what does the bowler target from the square leg position?
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a fielding position in cricket, which makes 'bowler' look like the cricket kind; it is the skittles player.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles a player rolling a ball tries to knock down the standing wooden targets.

clue.text: Complaint from a bishop during awkward chat

indicators.note: during puts the article and the bishop inside the rearranged chat
awkward means the letters of chat are put in an ungainly new order

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's illness comes up in an awkward conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges the letters of the chat word, and 'during' sets A plus RR, Right Reverend, inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and a build-up of mucus in the nose and throat is one.

clue.text: Band from Stoke essentially unchanged

indicators.note: essentially takes the central letter, the essence, of Stoke

parts.note: as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: A rock group from Stoke has stayed basically the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis were in fact a Manchester band, so 'from Stoke' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Britpop group led by the Gallagher brothers.

clue.text: Compromising one's art a capital offence?

indicators.note: compromising means damaging the integrity of something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist asks whether selling out their art is a hanging matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country was historically punishable by death, so it was a capital crime.

clue.text: When caught, forcibly ejects dog

indicators.note: when caught by the ear, the word for ejects sounds like the breed

parts.note: spits means forcibly ejects from the mouth

explanation.surface: A dog, when caught, forcibly spits something out.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dog with a pointed muzzle and curled tail, such as the Pomeranian type.

clue.text: Extra box with digit on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside puts the digit around the boxing word

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: An extra boxing bout with a finger outside the glove.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over beyond what is needed is surplus, available beyond the necessary.

clue.text: String in compact edition did its job

indicators.note: the letters strung together within the words compact edition hold the answer

explanation.surface: A string tied into a compact edition of a book worked as it should.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to function or perform, so having acted means having worked as intended.

clue.text: Small truck carrying right tool for decorator

indicators.note: carrying means the truck holds the right letter inside

parts.note: a tipper is a truck whose body tilts to unload

explanation.surface: A little lorry carries the right equipment for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraper or chemical for removing old paint or wallpaper is a painter's stock in trade.

clue.text: Talk up erstwhile turn of fate

parts.note: ex means former or erstwhile

indicators.note: turn of means the fate word is turned round

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Talking about a former twist of fate.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise warmly is to talk up, to boost by speaking highly of.

clue.text: What stops you lifting piece of lamb from cold store?

parts.note: something from a cold store is frozen
a shoulder is a joint of lamb

explanation.surface: A riddle about a joint of lamb taken from the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a medical condition in which the joint stiffens and arm movement is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff, painful joint condition limits arm movement, so raising things overhead becomes impossible.
